frozen_test.core_criterion: causal alteration of EXIT/resolution changes repair outcome
frozen_test.strict_cell_exit_counting_rule: count a tissue only when an intervention directly or near-directly changes persistence/clearance of a defined activated repair-state cell population and an objective repair outcome changes

counted_tissues.exit_effect: increased cleaved-caspase-3-positive cells and reduced alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblast persistence
counted_tissues.repair_effect: reduced scar burden in adult rat and mechanically loaded red Duroc pig wounds

counted_tissues.intervention: CD248-targeted BBIR-T cells against late-activated fibroblasts
counted_tissues.timing: treatment initiated at day 14 after myocardial infarction, when the scar was nearly mature; three injections at 3-day intervals
counted_tissues.exit_effect: approximately two-thirds reduction of CD248-positive late-activated fibroblasts after three injections
counted_tissues.repair_effect: reduced fibrosis expansion and adverse ventricular remodeling with improved cardiac function

counted_tissues.intervention: local diphtheria-toxin-induced apoptosis of Scx-lineage cells in Scx-Cre;Rosa-DTR mice
counted_tissues.timing: days 14-18 after flexor tendon repair, during the late proliferative/early remodeling interval
counted_tissues.exit_effect: direct depletion by apoptosis of Scx-lineage repair cells
counted_tissues.repair_effect: substantial structural and functional impairment at day 28; the mechanical deficit was transient and not significant by day 56
counted_tissues.interpretive_caveat: Scx-lineage cells are broader than the alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblast compartment, so this is a repair-state cell EXIT node rather than a myofibroblast-specific node.

timing_controls.finding: periostin-positive myofibroblasts are necessary for adaptive healing after myocardial infarction; early/ongoing ablation reduces scar formation and can compromise acute structural repair
timing_controls.role: supports a timing-dependent rather than monotonic EXIT model

timing_controls.finding: diphtheria-toxin-mediated ablation of periostin-expressing activated cardiac fibroblasts reduced fibrosis and improved function in post-MI and chronic angiotensin-II models without compromising scar stability in the reported MI protocol
timing_controls.role: independent causal replication that activated-fibroblast population control changes remodeling

supportive_but_not_counted_as_strict_cel.intervention: conditional depletion/reconstitution of monocyte-derived macrophages and MMP-13 competence
supportive_but_not_counted_as_strict_cel.repair_effect: matrix resolution is required for functional recovery
supportive_but_not_counted_as_strict_cel.reason_not_counted: causal target is scar-matrix resolution by resolving macrophages, not EXIT of the activated fibrogenic cell population

supportive_but_not_counted_as_strict_cel.intervention: inhibition of progeny generation by a scar-forming pericyte subclass
supportive_but_not_counted_as_strict_cel.repair_effect: reduced fibrosis/ECM deposition, enhanced axonal regeneration and sensorimotor recovery
supportive_but_not_counted_as_strict_cel.reason_not_counted: perturbs generation/expansion of scar-forming cells rather than their post-use clearance

best_supported_architecture: correctly timed and sufficiently selective EXIT/resolution
avoidance of persistent fibrosis without premature loss of repair capacity
gate_decision.interpretation: Skin, heart and tendon independently show that experimentally changing persistence/clearance of activated repair-state cells changes tissue outcome. The sign depends on timing and cell identity: late selective clearance can reduce persistent fibrosis, whereas depletion during a still-required repair window can impair recovery.

next_killer_test.target: measure tissue-specific repair-state decay constants and define the transition point at which cell persistence changes from adaptive to maladaptive
priority: skin: obtain intermediate in-vivo alpha-SMA/lineage timepoints after wound closure with and without FMOD
heart: reconstruct CD248-positive late-fibroblast decay after day-14 BBIR-T dosing
tendon: use published Scx/alpha-SMA D14-D42 trajectory plus depletion windows to bracket the safe EXIT onset
spinal cord: search for a direct late ablation/clearance experiment on scar-forming pericyte/fibroblast populations
